title: Plug-and-Pivot SDK Quicklaunch Notebook
content:
Purpose:
This is an experimental quicklaunch notebook for the SDK teams to get from checkout -> instrumented demo in under 30 minutes, with explicit fallback/pivot patterns for production integration. The goal is to reduce onboarding friction for internal integrators and early customers while providing a simple path to measure quality and cost tradeoffs.

Audience:
- SDK engineers building client libraries and integration examples
- Solutions engineers running customer pilots
- Field SEs who need a reproducible demo path

Key outcomes:
- Minimal reproducible app that calls Redwood API with streaming + fallback to local stub
- Instrumentation checklist that surfaces token cost, latency p50/p95, and prompt-regression counters
- Canary rollout checklist for model variant fallback (large->quantized->cached)

High-level flow (30m quickloop):
1) Clone starter repo and run local sandbox (3m)
   - git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter.git && cd sdk-starter
   - cp .env.example .env (paste REDWOOD_API_KEY)
   - ./dev up (starts local proxy and stub model)
2) Run the minimal sample app (5m)
   - python quickchat_demo.py --mode=stream --prompt-file=examples/promo.txt
   - Observe streaming output to console; confirm tokens and latency in local logs
3) Toggle to hosted backend and instrument (7m)
   - export BACKEND=hosted; ./dev restart-proxy
   - Run same sample, watch Console -> Observability panel for per-request metrics
4) Introduce a fallback policy and force a simulated failure (10m)
   - Modify config/fallback.yaml: primary: redwood/gpt-8, fallback: redwood/gpt-8-quant, final: local-stub
   - Simulate capacity error: curl -XPOST http://localhost:8080/simulate -d '{"type":"capacity"}'
   - Observe automatic routing to the quantized variant, then eventual local-stub when latency breaches 800ms

Telemetry & smoke checks (quick pass):
- stdout: confirm streaming chunk timestamps every ~100-200ms for first 3 tokens
- observability metrics: request_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate_usd, latency_ms_p50, latency_ms_p95
- prompt regression probe: run sample suite (tests/prompt-smoke/*.json) and assert >= 95% pass on hallucination checks

Canary rollout recipe (short):
- Phase A: 5% traffic to new SDK flow with feature flag ff/sdk-pilot-2026A for 48h
- Phase B: 20% after no regression alerts and latency delta < 15% vs baseline for 24h
- Phase C: 100% if error rate < 0.5% and cost delta acceptable
- Rollback: auto-fallback to previous pinned model + alert to #devx-oncall

Failure scenarios & quick debug notes (notes-to-self style):
- Proxy auth failures: check .env REDWOOD_API_KEY present and proxy logs show 401 -> rotate key and restart proxy
- Streaming stalls: confirm long-poll socket is active; if stall > 3s, switch to non-streaming path to capture body and surface partial results
- High token blowup on user prompts: run local prompt-sanitizer and enforce token cap 1024; log deltas to help prompt-engineering team

Developer ergonomics experiments (short list):
- Auto-warm KV cache on sdk init for anticipated system prompts (baseline experiment: warm 50 cached prefixes; measure p50 latency improvement)
- Local mode toggle in the SDK: "--local-first" that flips routing to local stub for quick offline demos
- One-command demo: ./dev demo --region=eu --model=fast-8 (creates ephemeral credentials + runs sample app)

Open questions / unresolved puzzles:
- How aggressive should the auto-fallback thresholds be for enterprise customers vs public tenants? (need input from product-hosted-api)
- Can we expose a safe "preview" cost estimate before streaming begins without doubling token decode work? (engineering research ticket?)

Quick checklist before sharing with SEs:
- [ ] update README with single-step env var export for REDWOOD_API_KEY
- [ ] add a small interactive troubleshooting section mapping common errors -> commands
- [ ] add prompt-smoke test suite to CI with a lightweight mock (GH action)
- [ ] link the demo to a recorded screencast for self-serve trials

Notes / links / references:
- Slack thread: #devx-quicklaunch (see pinned message)
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVEX/plug-and-pivot
- Related GH PR with sandbox updates: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482
- Jira ticket to track rollout and experiments: DEVEX-317

Quick log (mini-journal):
2025-11-03: initial scribble during hackday, rough flow validated with local stub
2025-12-09: added telemetry hooks; noticed streaming timestamp jitter on macOS CI runners
2026-02-18: implemented aggressive fallback prototype; observed 18% cost savings on a small pilot
2026-03-10: cleaned up commands and packaged demo into single ./dev script (current draft)

To do next (short):
- Draft a one-pager for Solutions with step-by-step screenshots (assigned to Asha)
- Run a 1-week SE pilot and capture feedback (Sofia to run)
- Open an engineering spike to evaluate early cost estimator accuracy (Liam)

End of notebook. If you rip anything for public docs, please sanitize internal IRIs and replace the demo API key with instructions to sign up for a trial account.
